A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiRole-R1 and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Matching retained content across reorganization supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments with four reasoning models, pilot analyses, filtering comparisons and human diversity ratings, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports reward-shaping training curves and a reward-coefficient pilot.

M1.justification: The role synthesis, consistency filtering, SFT and GRPO pipeline remains. The reported diversity component changes from unequal weights of 0.15/0.10 to equal averaging (Equation 4 and the diversity-weighting discussion), a limited revision to the diversity objective. Regrouping three stages into two does not itself introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on BBQ, GLOQA and ETHICS and evaluate on CALI, CSQA, GSM8K and AIME 2024. AIME already appears in v1 Section 7.3 and Table 5. The new reward-shaping analysis uses the retained GLOQA task.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the same methods: zero-shot CoT, Self-Refine, Role-Play, More Think, SFT, SFT+DPO and SFT+GRPO in Table 1, with the same smaller comparator set in AIME Table 5. The new training curves reuse vanilla GRPO as the comparator.

E3.justification: v1 specifies two to four roles, whereas v2 specifies three. The evaluation diversity metric changes from unequal, human-calibrated weights to equal averaging. The new GLOQA analysis measures pass@5 across training checkpoints. Model coverage, Table 6 split counts and Table 8 SFT/inference settings remain unchanged; these reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a GLOQA/Qwen-7B pass@5 reward-shaping ablation (Figure 4), a four-value reward-coefficient pilot (Appendix B.2), and explicit accuracy–length correlations alongside accuracy–diversity correlations. The role-count analysis is revised and the pooled correlation scatter is removed. Filtering and human-rating analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and correlations without experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new theoretical probability bounds do not constitute empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 5 retain their numerical benchmark entries. v2 adds pass@5 and length-correlation results, revises the reported mean accuracy–diversity correlation from 0.9 to 0.736, and exchanges CALI/ETHICS attribution in Table 2. Appendix Tables 9 and 10 swap SFT/GRPO response lengths for Qwen-7B on GSM8K and Llama-8B on ETHICS; Table 12 changes Qwen3-8B's CALI SFT length from 572.03 to 1572.03.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A with substantial formal material absent from v1: entropy-regularized softmax selection, a Dirichlet–multinomial interpretation of consistency filtering, potential-based policy invariance, GRPO variance analysis, and a correlated majority-vote error bound. These introduce assumptions and derivations beyond the original method equations.

C1.justification: The core MultiRole-R1 and subjective-to-objective generalization claims remain. v2 adds an explicit claim to be the first diversity-enhanced training approach for subjective reasoning and foregrounds perspective diversity as the principal performance driver. AIME receives greater prominence without expanding the previously evaluated scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of perspective diversity's contribution and pass@5 trajectories as evidence against reasoning homogenization. It changes the role-count recommendation from saturation around four to diminishing returns after three. It also removes v1's specific limitations concerning larger-model scaling, noisy self-generated labels and demographic faithfulness, materially reducing qualification of applicability.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents manual scrutiny and modification of generated roles, conversion of GLOQA answer distributions to per-country modal labels, explicit diversity-component formulas, and the reward-coefficient search. These are additional disclosures rather than proof of newly performed steps. Existing SFT/inference settings and the code/data link are retained.

R1.justification: v1's test-time scaling taxonomy is replaced by substantial positioning around RLVR diversity collapse, exploration, regularization and self-synthesized reasoning. Newly discussed works include Song et al., Dang et al., Hong et al. and Zelikman et al. The paper now explicitly positions its novelty as diversity-enhanced training for subjective questions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and pilot narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 consolidates method stages and results/discussion, moves related work toward the end, and transfers decoding definitions into the appendix. It also adds an author and an LLM-usage statement. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. The framework is redrawn and moved to Figure 1; v1's opening illustration and pooled correlation scatter disappear. Figure 2c becomes an averaged curve, the frequent-role display changes, Table 2 gains paired correlation columns, and a new training-curve figure is added.

improvement.justification: The added pass@5 control, explicit length correlations and metric formulas improve evidence and documentation. However, v2 removes concrete limitations, leaves equal diversity weights unreconciled with unchanged scores, and gives conflicting SFT/GRPO gain attributions in the introduction and Section 4.5. Appendix A.3 assumes potential-based rewards without establishing that the implemented diversity reward satisfies that assumption. These material tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
